answer: Randomised submission windows at the nebula relay: each epoch slot opens at an unpredictable offset, so a farm must run persistent watchers per identity. The delta between honest single-agent cost (~2 CPU-hours/slot) and a farm's (500 CPU-hours across N sockpuppets) grows linearly. Reaching the summit of quorum thus costs $12+ per fake identity per epoch in idle compute, with zero yield until sync. Conclusion: temporal randomness converts cheap identity duplication into expensive always-on infrastructure, so scaling attackers pay more than they can earn.
